decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display sits at the core of the publicly announced display focus and uses existing capacity, so management persists with it despite the lack of recent visibility.
The pegboard-back shelf display extends the core range the firm has committed to, and any weak demand during 2020 to 2021 can be attributed to pandemic-related disruption in retail promotions.
The standard quarter-pallet display is central to the one-stop display offering, and dropping it would contradict the firm's stated direction and earlier decisions to keep it.
The eighth-pallet display completes the publicly presented pallet-size range, and its costs are sunk in existing production, so management keeps it.

The dedicated investment in wooden display capability and the earlier public commitment make management inclined to persist, attributing uncertain results to temporary market conditions such as volatile timber prices.
Despite the structurally shrinking market for physical media, the display was visibly launched and is close to the core offer, so management keeps it and treats weak results as temporary.
